guide.summary: Todoist API v1 documents user-authorized OAuth2 for third-party apps, and data:read is the documented read-only scope covering tasks. Listing active tasks uses GET /api/v1/tasks with cursor pagination, so no write scope is selected.

findings.appliesWhen: The customer connects their own Todoist account through the app.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. It does not grant create, update, complete or delete operations, and it is the least-privilege documented scope for listing active tasks.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles from the connected person's account via GET /api/v1/tasks.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Token exchange and refresh are required for ongoing access
findings.detail: After authorization, the app exchanges the code at the token endpoint. For apps with refresh tokens enabled, which is the default for newly created apps, the response includes expires_in and refresh_token, and expired access tokens are refreshed via the token endpoint.
findings.appliesWhen: Every connected customer account once the access token expires.

steps.title: Register the Todoist OAuth application and configure redirect URL
steps.detail: Developer creates a Todoist application in the App Management Console, configures a valid OAuth2 redirect URL, and receives a Client ID and Client Secret. Consent and token exchange are executed later; this step only prepares the app.
steps.doneWhen: Application exists with a Client ID, Client Secret, and redirect URL recorded for the test environment.

steps.title: Use the read-only data:read scope and consent redirect
steps.detail: Customer is redirected to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, scope=data:read and state, then the callback is checked for the returned code and matching state before any token exchange.
steps.doneWhen: Callback returns a code with the matching state value and the consent shows data:read only.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize , with the specified request parameters.

fields: client_id from the registered app
state is a random value generated by the developer
code returned in the callback query string

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the callback code at the documented token endpoint. Documented client_secret_post authentication uses client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri as form fields.
steps.doneWhen: Response is HTTP 200 with access_token and token_type Bearer, plus refresh_token and expires_in when refresh tokens are enabled.

fields: client_id from the registered app
client_secret from the registered app
code from the callback query string
redirect_uri matching the registered redirect URL

steps.title: Read the first page of active tasks
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the Bearer token and limit to retrieve the first page. Read each results[].content as a task title and keep next_cursor for continuation.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 response whose results array contains content strings and a next_cursor value or null. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN from the token exchange response
Task title is results[].content

steps.title: Confirm read-only boundary with the data:read grant
steps.detail: Verify the connected app grant is data:read only and that no create, update, complete or delete request is issued. Inspect the granted scope in the consent screen and outgoing request log; do not execute any write.
steps.doneWhen: Grant shows data:read only and the request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/tasks.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

steps.title: Fetch the next page of active tasks using next_cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same GET /api/v1/tasks request with the same limit and pass next_cursor as cursor. Continue until next_cursor is null, which is the documented end condition.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched until next_cursor is null and all task titles are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?cursor=eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6NTB9.aGFzaA&limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
} When next_cursor is null , you've reached the end of the results.
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :

fields: NEXT_CURSOR comes from next_cursor in the prior response
Use identical limit and parameters on every page
